content: Excessive alcohol consumption during pregnancy is linked to harmful effects on both the mother and the newborn. It is crucial to develop and assess effective interventions during this critical period in a woman's life. To date, no systematic reviews of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) have been conducted in this specific population. The objective of this study was to evaluate the effectiveness of pharmacologic interventions in pregnant women enrolled in alcohol treatment programs. The focus was on improving birth and neonatal outcomes, promoting maternal abstinence from alcohol, and enhancing retention in treatment programs. To identify relevant studies, a comprehensive search was conducted across multiple databases, including the Cochrane Drugs and Alcohol Group's Trial Register (as of August 2008), MEDLINE (from 1950 to June 2008), EMBASE (from 1974 to August 2008), CINAHL (from 1982 to June 2008), and PsycInfo (from 1806 to June 2008). Additionally, reference lists of articles were manually searched for further relevant studies. The inclusion criteria required randomized or quasi-randomized studies that compared any pharmacologic intervention with other pharmacologic treatments, either alone or in combination with psychosocial treatment, placebo, non-intervention, or psychosocial intervention. Two independent reviewers assessed the identified trials for inclusion in the review. Standardized data extraction and quality assessment forms were to be used for eligible studies. However, no suitable trials were identified for inclusion. The search strategy yielded 793 citations. Of these, 23 citations were selected for full-text review. An additional 10 articles were identified through manual reference searches, resulting in a total of 33 articles for full-text review. Despite this extensive search, no studies met the inclusion criteria. Consequently, data extraction and methodological quality assessment could not be performed. The authors concluded that the research question remains unanswered due to the absence of relevant randomized controlled trials. There is a pressing need for high-quality research to evaluate the effectiveness of pharmacologic interventions in pregnant women enrolled in alcohol treatment programs.
